newsitem.title: INDIA: ING Barings says Indian stocks yet to bottom out.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings says Indian stocks yet to bottom out.

text.p: Indian stock markets, which gave up on Thursday nearly one-third of its previous day's gain, will take more time to emerge from a slump, a top broking firm said.
"We continue to believe that the bear phase has not yet run its full course," said ING Barings in a note on Thursday.
"It is a good opportunity to restructure portfolios and get rid of cement/auto stocks."
The benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange top-30 shares index fell 58.80 points, or 2.0 percent, to 2,882.56 at provisional close on Thursday, after rebounding 5.1 percent on Wednesday.
The broking firm said Wednesday's rebound was sparked by hopes of economic revival and some government incentives in the first quarter of 1997.
"(Such) hopes will be belied as fundamentals continue to deteriorate," it said.
